title: Ezekiel Chapter 37 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 37 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 37 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 37.

questions.question: Where did the LORD set Ezekiel down in the spirit of the LORD?
options: In the midst of the valley full of bones
questions.correctAnswer: In the midst of the valley full of bones
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:1 states that the hand of the LORD carried Ezekiel out in the spirit of the LORD and set him down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones.

questions.question: What was notable about the bones in the valley?
questions.correctAnswer: They were very dry
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:2 describes the bones as very many and very dry in the open valley.

questions.question: What question did God ask Ezekiel about the bones?
options: Do these bones belong to Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Can these bones live?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:3 records God asking Ezekiel if the bones can live.

questions.question: What did God command Ezekiel to do to the dry bones?
options: Prophesy upon them and say, 'O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD'
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesy upon them and say, 'O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD'
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:4 commands Ezekiel to prophesy upon the dry bones and speak the word of the LORD to them.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would cause to enter into the bones so they would live?
questions.correctAnswer: Breath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:5 states that the LORD will cause breath to enter into the bones so they shall live.

questions.question: Which of the following did the LORD say He would put on the bones?
questions.correctAnswer: Sinews, flesh, skin, and breath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:6 explains that the LORD will lay sinews on the bones, bring up flesh, cover them with skin, and put breath in them.

questions.question: What happened when Ezekiel prophesied as commanded to the bones?
options: There was a noise and shaking; the bones came together bone to his bone
questions.correctAnswer: There was a noise and shaking; the bones came together bone to his bone
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:7 describes a noise and shaking as the bones came together bone to his bone when Ezekiel prophesied.

questions.question: After the bones came together and flesh covered them, what was still missing?
questions.correctAnswer: Breath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:8 says the sinews, flesh, and skin covered the bones, but there was no breath in them.

questions.question: To what did God tell Ezekiel to prophesy next?
questions.correctAnswer: To the wind
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:9 directs Ezekiel to prophesy to the wind and command it to breathe upon the slain that they may live.

questions.question: What was the result when Ezekiel prophesied to the wind?
options: The breath came into them and they lived and stood up as a great army
questions.correctAnswer: The breath came into them and they lived and stood up as a great army
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:10 states the breath came into the bones, they lived, and stood up upon their feet as an exceeding great army.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 37:11 says the dry bones represent the whole house of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11 explicitly says the bones are the whole house of Israel, who say their bones are dried and hope is lost.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said He would make the children of Israel two separate nations forever.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:22 states that the LORD will make them one nation with one king and no longer divided into two kingdoms.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 37:24, David shall be king over the united nation of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:24 says David my servant shall be king over them, and they shall have one shepherd.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 37:26 speaks of an everlasting covenant of peace made with Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:26 declares God will make a covenant of peace with Israel that is everlasting.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 37, which instruction comes first?
options: Gather the children of Israel from the heathen
Open the graves of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesy upon the dry bones
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:4 commands Ezekiel first to prophesy upon the dry bones before later instructions such as joining sticks or gathering Israel.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 37 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 37 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 37:11, what do the dry bones represent?
questions.correctAnswer: The whole house of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11 states that the bones represent the whole house of Israel, who feel their hope is lost and that they are cut off.

questions.question: What promise does God make to His people in Ezekiel 37:12?
options: He will open their graves and bring them into the land of Israel
He will send a prophet to lead them
He will give them wealth and power
He will make them kings over the nations
questions.correctAnswer: He will open their graves and bring them into the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:12 promises that God will open the graves of His people and bring them back into the land of Israel.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 37:14 describe God's action toward His people after bringing them up from the graves?
options: He will put His spirit in them and they shall live
He will make them rulers over other nations
He will send them into exile again
questions.correctAnswer: He will put His spirit in them and they shall live
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:14 states that God will put His spirit in His people so they may live and be settled in their own land.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 37:16, what are the two sticks that Ezekiel is commanded to write upon?
options: For Judah and for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: For Judah and for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:16 commands Ezekiel to write on one stick for Judah and his companions, and on another for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all Israel's companions.

questions.question: What is the significance of joining the two sticks into one, according to Ezekiel 37:17?
options: They shall become one in Ezekiel's hand, symbolizing unity
They will become a weapon in battle
They will be thrown into the fire as a sign of judgment
They will be sent separately to different nations
questions.correctAnswer: They shall become one in Ezekiel's hand, symbolizing unity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:17 explains that joining the two sticks symbolizes the uniting of the divided kingdoms into one.

questions.question: What question do the children of Ezekiel's people ask him in Ezekiel 37:18?
options: Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these?
Why do the bones remain dry?
questions.correctAnswer: Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these?
questions.explanation: Verse 18 records the people asking Ezekiel to explain the meaning of the two sticks and their joining.

questions.question: How does God explain the meaning of the two sticks in Ezekiel 37:19?
options: He will join the stick of Joseph with the stick of Judah to make one stick
He will destroy both sticks as a symbol of judgment
He will give the sticks to different nations
He will write new names on the sticks
questions.correctAnswer: He will join the stick of Joseph with the stick of Judah to make one stick
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:19 clarifies that God will unite the tribes represented by the two sticks into one nation under His hand.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 37:20, where will Ezekiel hold the sticks?
options: In his hand before their eyes
Buried in the valley of dry bones
questions.correctAnswer: In his hand before their eyes
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states the sticks will be held by Ezekiel visibly before the people as a symbol.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 37:21 say God will do with the children of Israel?
options: Gather them from the nations and bring them into their own land
Scatter them further among the heathen
Make them rulers over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Gather them from the nations and bring them into their own land
questions.explanation: God promises in verse 21 to gather Israel from among the nations and bring them back to their land.

questions.question: What will happen to the nation of Israel according to Ezekiel 37:22?
options: They will be one nation with one king and no longer divided
They will be divided into many kingdoms
They will be conquered by foreign powers
They will remain in exile forever
questions.correctAnswer: They will be one nation with one king and no longer divided
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:22 promises that Israel will be united as one nation with one king and no longer divided.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 37:22-23, how does God describe the spiritual state of the united nation?
options: They shall no longer defile themselves with idols and transgressions
They will be indifferent to God's laws
They will continue in sin without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They shall no longer defile themselves with idols and transgressions
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 state that the united nation will be cleansed, refrain from idolatry, and be God's people.

questions.question: Who is identified as king over the united Israel in Ezekiel 37:24?
questions.correctAnswer: David my servant
questions.explanation: Verse 24 says that David, God's servant, shall be king and shepherd over the united people.

questions.question: Ezekiel 37:25 promises that the people will dwell in the land given to whom?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob my servant
questions.explanation: The verse affirms that the people will live in the land given to Jacob, their forefather, and their descendants.

questions.question: What covenant does God make with Israel according to Ezekiel 37:26?
questions.correctAnswer: An everlasting covenant of peace
questions.explanation: Verse 26 promises God will establish an everlasting covenant of peace with His people.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 37:13 teaches that the people will know the LORD when He opens their graves and brings them up.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:13 explicitly states that the people will know the LORD when He brings them up from their graves.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 37 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 37.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 37:21, from where will the Lord gather the children of Israel?
options: From among the heathen, whither they be gone
questions.correctAnswer: From among the heathen, whither they be gone
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:21 states that God will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, wherever they have gone, and gather them on every side into their own land.

questions.question: What will God do to the nation of Israel in Ezekiel 37:22?
options: Make them one nation with one king
Divide them into two kingdoms again
questions.correctAnswer: Make them one nation with one king
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:22 prophesies that God will make Israel one nation in their land with one king, ending their division into two kingdoms.

questions.question: Which of the following will the people of Israel no longer defile themselves with, according to Ezekiel 37:23?
questions.correctAnswer: Idols, detestable things, and transgressions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:23 specifies that Israel shall no longer defile themselves with idols, detestable things, or their sins, as God will cleanse and save them.

questions.question: Who is described as 'my servant' and the future king over Israel in Ezekiel 37:24?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:24 declares that David, God's servant, shall be king over the reunited Israel and shepherd them under God's statutes.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 37:25, where will the people of Israel dwell forever?
options: In the land given to Jacob, their fathers' land
questions.correctAnswer: In the land given to Jacob, their fathers' land
questions.explanation: The verse states that Israel will dwell in the land given to Jacob, their ancestor, along with their descendants forever.

questions.question: What kind of covenant will God make with Israel according to Ezekiel 37:26?
questions.correctAnswer: An everlasting covenant of peace
questions.explanation: God promises an everlasting covenant of peace with Israel in Ezekiel 37:26, including His sanctuary being among them forever.

questions.question: What will God place in the midst of Israel forever as per Ezekiel 37:27?
questions.correctAnswer: His tabernacle
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:27 states God's tabernacle will be with Israel, symbolizing His presence and their identity as His people.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 37:28, what will the heathen know when God's sanctuary is in the midst of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD sanctifies Israel
questions.explanation: The verse reveals that the nations will recognize God's sanctification of Israel when His sanctuary dwells among them forever.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Ezekiel 37:16-17 with the two sticks representing Judah and Joseph?
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolism
questions.explanation: The two sticks symbolize the divided kingdoms of Israel being joined into one, a clear use of symbolism in Ezekiel 37:16-17.

questions.question: The phrase 'one king shall be king to them all' in Ezekiel 37:22 foreshadows which New Testament figure?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: The prophecy of a single king over Israel points forward to Jesus Christ, who is recognized as the Messiah and King in the New Testament (cf. Luke 1:32).

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'breath' or 'spirit' is central to the vision of dry bones in Ezekiel 37:5-6 and also signifies life?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruach
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ruach' (spirit or breath) is used in Ezekiel 37 to represent the life-giving power of God breathed into the dry bones.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage shares the theme of God restoring Israel from death to life, similar to Ezekiel 37?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 143:5
questions.explanation: Psalm 143:5 speaks of remembering the ancient days and thinking of all God's works, including revival, paralleling Ezekiel's vision of restoration.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 37:24, the people of Israel will have many shepherds ruling over them after their restoration.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:24 clearly states they shall have one shepherd, David, ruling over them, not many.

questions.question: True or False: The joining of the two sticks in Ezekiel 37:17 symbolizes the permanent reunification of Israel and Judah into one kingdom.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The joining of sticks in Ezekiel 37:17 symbolizes the future unity of Israel and Judah under one nation and king, fulfilling God's promise.

questions.question: What future event in Ezekiel 37:26-27 indicates God's permanent presence among His people?
options: Setting His sanctuary in their midst forever
Building a new temple in Babylon
Sending prophets to warn them annually
questions.correctAnswer: Setting His sanctuary in their midst forever
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:26-27 describes God placing His sanctuary in the midst of Israel forever, indicating His abiding presence.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 37 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 37 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the valley full of dry bones represent according to Ezekiel 37:11?
questions.correctAnswer: The whole house of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11 states that the bones represent the whole house of Israel, who feel their hope is lost and that they are cut off.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 37:5-6, what divine act is God promising to perform on the dry bones?
options: Cause breath to enter them so they will live
questions.correctAnswer: Cause breath to enter them so they will live
questions.explanation: God promises in Ezekiel 37:5-6 to cause breath to enter the dry bones so they will live, bringing sinews, flesh, and skin upon them.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is primarily illustrated by the vision of the dry bones coming to life (Ezekiel 37:1-10)?
options: The doctrine of resurrection and spiritual renewal
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of resurrection and spiritual renewal
questions.explanation: The vision in Ezekiel 37:1-10 symbolizes God's power to give life to what is dead, teaching resurrection and spiritual renewal as God breathes life into the bones.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 37:16-17, what is the significance of joining the two sticks representing Judah and Joseph?
options: They symbolize the reunification of divided Israel
They represent two opposing kingdoms forever separated
They foretell the destruction of Israel
They indicate the exile of Israel and Judah
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize the reunification of divided Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:16-17 indicates that joining the sticks symbolizes God’s promise to unify Judah and Joseph’s tribes into one nation again.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 37:12-14 when God promises to open graves and put His spirit into the people?
options: God's power to give life and restore
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to give life and restore
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:12-14 reveals God’s power to restore life by opening graves and putting His spirit in His people, illustrating His life-giving and restorative nature.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 37:23 teach about the sanctification process God will bring about in Israel?
options: Israel will no longer defile themselves with idols and transgressions
Israel will remain in their sinful ways
Israel will be abandoned by God
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will no longer defile themselves with idols and transgressions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:23 states that God will cleanse Israel so they will no longer defile themselves with idols or sins, indicating a sanctification process.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 37:24-25 connect to the Messianic hope in the broader redemptive narrative?
options: David (a type of Messiah) will be king over unified Israel forever
Israel will remain leaderless and divided
A foreign king will rule Israel
questions.correctAnswer: David (a type of Messiah) will be king over unified Israel forever
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:24-25 points to the Messianic hope of a Davidic king ruling a united Israel eternally, connecting to the promise of Christ’s eternal reign.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 37:26-27 reveal about God's covenant relationship with His people?
options: God will make an everlasting covenant of peace and dwell among His people
God will reject His people forever
God will allow them to be scattered indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: God will make an everlasting covenant of peace and dwell among His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:26-27 teaches that God will establish an everlasting covenant of peace and place His sanctuary among His people, emphasizing His commitment to fellowship and presence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the vision of dry bones is merely a myth with no real promise of restoration. What does Ezekiel 37:21-22 actually teach about Israel’s future?
options: God will gather Israel from the nations and unite them as one nation with one king
Israel will remain scattered and divided forever
The vision was only symbolic with no real fulfillment
questions.correctAnswer: God will gather Israel from the nations and unite them as one nation with one king
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:21-22 clearly teaches God's promise to gather Israel from exile and unify them, showing a real future restoration contrary to sceptical claims.

questions.question: Which combined doctrinal insight does Ezekiel 37:5-6 and 37:14 provide about the role of God's Spirit in salvation?
options: God's Spirit brings life and enables living, restoring both body and soul
God's Spirit creates physical bones only
questions.correctAnswer: God's Spirit brings life and enables living, restoring both body and soul
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:5-6 shows God breathing life into dry bones, and 37:14 states He will put His Spirit in people so they shall live, teaching the Spirit’s role in full restoration and life.

questions.question: What theological truth about God's sovereignty is illustrated by the command to prophesy to the wind in Ezekiel 37:9-10?
options: God controls the elements and gives life by His Spirit
God is limited by natural forces
questions.correctAnswer: God controls the elements and gives life by His Spirit
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:9-10 shows that God commands the wind (breath/spirit) to come and give life, demonstrating His sovereign control over creation and life-giving power.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 37:16-20 and 37:21-22 together depict God's plan for Israel's unity and identity?
options: God will unite the divided tribes into one nation under one king
God will keep Israel divided and scattered
God will replace Israel with a new nation
questions.correctAnswer: God will unite the divided tribes into one nation under one king
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:16-20 symbolize uniting Judah and Joseph’s sticks, and 37:21-22 confirm God’s plan to gather Israel into one nation with one king, emphasizing unity and restoration.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in Ezekiel 37:28 where it says the heathen shall know that God sanctifies Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and sanctifying power
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:28 declares that God sanctifies Israel and His sanctuary will be among them forever, highlighting His holiness and sanctifying nature.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the promise in Ezekiel 37:25 regarding the land that God has given to Jacob?
options: The doctrine of the eternal inheritance and covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the eternal inheritance and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:25 promises that Israel and their descendants will dwell in the land given to Jacob forever, teaching God's faithful covenant and eternal inheritance.

questions.question: What is the significance of David being called 'my servant' and 'prince forever' in Ezekiel 37:24-25 in Christological terms?
options: It foreshadows the Messiah who will reign eternally from David’s line
It indicates David’s historical kingship only
It denies any future kingly reign
It refers to a foreign ruler
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the Messiah who will reign eternally from David’s line
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:24-25’s reference to David as servant and eternal prince foreshadows Christ, the Messiah from David’s lineage who reigns forever.
